news_title: Product safety recalls - 23 667 Chery Tiggo 4, Omoda C5 and Chery Tiggo 8 Pro Max 2.0 vehicles - The National Consumer Commission (NCC)
efet_title: Product safety recalls - 23 667 Chery Tiggo 4, Omoda C5 and Chery Tiggo 8 Pro Max 2.0 vehicles - The National Consumer Commission
efet_body:
Product safety recalls – 23 667 Chery Tiggo 4, Omoda C5 and Chery Tiggo 8 Pro Max 2.0 vehicles
Date Posted:
November 10, 2026
The National Consumer Commission (NCC) notifies consumers of a recall affecting a total of 23 667 (twenty-three thousand, six hundred and sixty-seven) vehicles as notified by Chery International (Pty) Ltd trading as Chery South Africa (Chery). The recall affects Chery Tiggo 4, Omoda C5 and Chery Tiggo 8 Pro Max 2.0 vehicles.
CHERY TIGGO 4 – 17 508
VEHICLES
Chery informed the NCC that this recall affects 17 508 (seventeen thousand five hundred and eight) vehicles made available for sale between 17 October 2023 and 27 March 2024. These vehicles were sold nationally. According to the supplier, the affected vehicles may have welding irregularities at the rear axle sleeve. This could cause the rear axle to dislodge, resulting in rear suspension collapse.
CHERY TIGGO 8 PRO MAX 2.0 – 3 474 VEHICLES
Chery is recalling certain Chery Tiggo 8 Pro Max 2.0 vehicles manufactured from 20 May 2026 onwards, affecting 3 474 (three thousand four hundred and seventy-four) vehicles. According to the supplier, the front brake-pipe may contact the turbocharger assembly, causing wear and potential brake-fluid leakage. This could reduce braking performance and increase stopping distances, potentially resulting in a collision, serious injury or death.
OMODA C5 – 2 685 VEHICLES
Chery is also recalling 2 685 (two thousand six hundred and eighty-five) Omoda C5 vehicles. These vehicles were made available for sale between February 2023 and July 2026, nationally. According to the supplier, the rear axle sleeve may have welding defects. This could cause the rear axle to dislodge, resulting in rear suspension collapse.
Consumers are urged to visit their authorised dealerships for an inspection and possible repairs, visit Chery’s website to verify if the VIN member is affected or if it is unsafe to drive the affected motor vehicle contact Chery’s authorised dealerships or their contact centre to arrange towing. Any remedial work will be carried out at no cost to the consumer.
NCC Acting Commissioner, Mr Hardin Ratshisusu, said: “Whilst we urge consumers to heed the call and respond to this recall, we also remind suppliers of their obligation to notify any product recall promptly. To this end, the NCC initiated a separate investigation against Chery in October 2026 over allegations that certain vehicles were recalled without informing the NCC, which investigation is ongoing.”
Questions and queries relating to this recall may be directed to:
ProductRecall@thencc.org.za
.
Ends

efet_title: Media Statement: Deli Hummus range Product Safety Recall - The National Consumer Commission
efet_body:
Media Statement: Deli Hummus range Product Safety Recall
Date Posted:
October 3, 2024
On 16 September 2024, Shoprite Checkers notified the Consumer Commission (NCC) of a product recall of the Deli Hummus range manufactured by BM Foods (a member of Sea Harvest Group), following the detection of Listeria Monocytogenes which is a species of foodborne bacteria.
The affected products are the Deli Hummus range, specifically the following:
Traditional Hummus (125g and 300g);
Reduced Fat Hummus (125g);
Zataar Hummus (125g and 300g);
Red Pepper Hummus (125g and 300g); and
Caramelised Onion Hummus (125g).
The respective sell-by dates of the products are 10 September 2024 to 08 October 2024.
Subsequent to the product recall notification, and in line with Section 60 of the Consumer Protection Act 68 of 2008, Shoprite Checkers has now provided an interim Investigation Report to the NCC on the Deli Hummus range. The preliminary findings of the report point to some areas of concern on product handling at the manufacturing level, however, the NCC awaits a final report from Shoprite Checkers. Parallel to the said in-house processes, the NCC is independently investigating the recalled products on identified operational issues that pertain to food safety.
The NCC’s Acting Commissioner, Mr. Hardin Ratshisusu, urged consumers to immediately stop consuming the products and return same to the supplier for a full refund with or without any proof of purchase. He further added that “at this stage, the NCC is not able to determine the extent of the distribution of the products as this is the subject of an investigation. Suppliers are urged not to distribute these products further until the investigation is finalised.”
The NCC is monitoring this recall based on the Product Recall provisions of the Consumer Protection Action read with the product recall safety guidelines.
ENDS
Issued by: National Consumer Commission (NCC)

news_title: Judgment due in Duduzile Zuma-Sambudla's bid to have terrorism-related charges withdrawn - EWN
efet_title: Judgment due in Duduzile Zuma-Sambudla's bid to have terrorism-related charges withdrawn - EWN
efet_body:
Judgment in Duduzile Zuma-Sambudla’s application to have terrorism-related charges against her withdrawn is due on Friday at the Durban High Court.
The former president's daughter was charged last year, accused of incitement to commit terrorism and public violence.
ALSO READ:
Zuma-Sambudla’s lawyers: It’s ‘laughable’ social media posts incited July unrest violence
NPA argues reasonable grounds for Zuma-Sambudla to be convicted over July unrest
Zuma-Sambudla's social media account played significant role in lead-up to July unrest, court hears
This, over her social media posts during the July 2021 unrest.
In the wake of Jacob Zuma's arrest, due to his absence from the State Capture Commission, a wave of public violence spread across KwaZulu-Natal and Gauteng in July of 2021.
At the time, Zuma-Sambudla reposted images and videos of the violence on X, captioned "Amandla" and "We See You".
She insists this was simply a greeting, with Advocate Dali Mpofu noting that the State's evidence was laughable. They applied in October to have the matter discharged.
But the State referred to Zuma-Sambudla’s influence at the time, despite conceding that legal parameters around social media and what constitutes offences were still developing here at home and around the globe.
Meanwhile, the 44-year-old remains expelled from her father's uMkhonto weSizwe (MK) Party.
